ai.description: *Micrixalus nigraventris* is a small frog (20–25 mm) with a brown dorsum and distinctive jet-black belly. It is identified by its slender build and the male's characteristic foot-flagging behavior.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus nigraventris* is uniquely distinguished from other dancing frogs by its distinct, solid black belly, which lacks the white or mottled patterns seen in relatives.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus nigraventris* inhabits fast-flowing, rocky streams within evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 500 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: To attract mates, male *Micrixalus nigraventris* perform a unique "foot-flagging" display, rhythmically extending and waving their hind legs against the backdrop of forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus nigraventris* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of unpigmented eggs in hidden nests beneath stream-bed gravel.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Micrixalus nigraventris* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the states of Karnataka and Kerala at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Black-bellied Dancing Frog emits a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short, metallic chirps while perched near fast-flowing, rocky streams in the Western Ghats.
